entities.summary: Thibaud of Ostia was a French cardinal who played a crucial role in the politics of Western Europe during the 12th century. Born into a noble family, Thibaud rose to prominence through his connections with the Catholic Church and his involvement in the governance of the Catholic Church. He served as a cardinal and a diplomat, mediating between the Holy Roman Empire and the Kingdom of France. Thibaud's efforts helped to stabilize the region and secure the interests of the Catholic Church. His legacy can be seen in the numerous churches and monasteries he helped to establish, which continue to play an important role in the cultural and spiritual life of Western Europe. Despite his significant contributions, Thibaud's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and his exact dates of birth and death are unknown.
